description: Fix form name mismatch and prefill issues caused by duplicate keys and inconsistent field ID mappings in server.js LABEL_TO_FIELD
steps: Step 1: Create new branch from origin/main. Run: git checkout origin/main && git checkout -b feat/form-fixes-and-talktime-widget

Step 2: Fix LABEL_TO_FIELD duplicate keys in server.js (around line 1200-1310). The problem: JS object literal duplicate keys mean the last one wins. 'Business name' maps to f_company (last) but BL_Business uses f_biz_name. 'Business address' maps to f_office_addr (last) but BL_Business uses f_biz_addr. Fix by making these form-type-aware. The approach: since labels in Applicant_Info.txt differ by form (BL writes 'Business Name' with capital N, PL/LAP write 'Business name' with lowercase n), use exact case to distinguish: 'Business Name' -> f_biz_name (BL_Business), 'Business name' -> f_company (PL/LAP). For addresses: BL writes 'Business Address' (capital A in section header context) but actually writes 'Business Address   :' - check the exact output labels in BL_Business.html line 943. Actually BL outputs 'Business Address' and PL/LAP output 'Business address'. Use case sensitivity. ALTERNATIVELY and more robustly: remove the duplicate keys entirely and instead add form-type-specific label variants. The cleanest fix: keep the FIRST occurrence of each key that maps correctly for BL_Business (which is the only form using f_biz_name/f_biz_addr), and ADD new distinctly-cased entries for the LAP/PL forms. Specifically: 'Business Name' (capital N as BL writes it) -> f_biz_name, 'Business name' (lowercase n as PL/LAP write it) -> f_company. 'Business Address' (capital A as BL writes it) -> f_biz_addr, 'Business address' (lowercase a as PL/LAP write it) -> f_office_addr.

Step 3: Fix Agent name mapping. Currently: 'Agent name' (lowercase n) -> f_bank, 'Agent Name' (capital N) -> f_agent. BL_Business uses f_agent and writes 'Agent name' (lowercase n) in its text output (line 900). The other 4 forms use f_bank and also write 'Agent name' (lowercase n). So when server reads 'Agent name' it currently maps to f_bank which is CORRECT for PL/LAP forms but WRONG for BL. The fix: BL_Business should write a distinct label in its text output OR we fix the HTML field id. The simplest fix: change BL_Business.html to use id='f_bank' for its agent name field (matching all other forms) OR change BL_Business's text output to use 'Agent Name' (capital N). Since BL_Business's HTML label says 'Agent Name' (capital N) and its field is f_agent, the cleanest fix is: change BL_Business's Applicant_Info.txt output on line 900 from 'Agent name' to 'Agent Name' so it maps correctly to f_agent via the LABEL_TO_FIELD entry 'Agent Name': 'f_agent'. BUT WAIT - all 5 forms should be CONSISTENT. The real issue is that BL_Business uses id='f_agent' while ALL other forms use id='f_bank' for the same conceptual field. The BEST fix: standardize BL_Business to use f_bank like the others. Change BL_Business.html: id='f_agent' -> id='f_bank', and update its text output reference from val('f_agent') to val('f_bank'). Then remove 'Agent Name': 'f_agent' from LABEL_TO_FIELD (no longer needed). Keep 'Agent name': 'f_bank'.

Step 4: Fix the 'Residence to Business Distance' mapping. BL_Business uses id='f_distance' and outputs label 'Residence to Business Distance'. PL/LAP use id='f_biz_distance' and output 'Res. to biz. dist.' or 'Res-to-biz dist'. In LABEL_TO_FIELD: 'Residence to Business Distance': 'f_distance' is correct for BL. 'Res. to biz. dist.': 'f_biz_distance' is correct for PL/LAP. This mapping is already correct - verify no changes needed here.

Step 5: Verify the lead-shared.js fuzzy label matching. The prefillFromInfoFields function does substring matching which could incorrectly match 'Full name' to fields labeled 'Father's name' or 'Mother's name' or 'Business name'. Check if there are safeguards. The normLabel function strips non-alphanumeric chars. 'full name' vs 'father s name' - these don't substring-match each other since 'full name' is not contained in 'father s name' and vice versa. But 'name' (if a label is just 'Name' as used for references at lines 928/934) could match 'Full name'. The fix: in lead-shared.js prefillFromInfoFields, add a minimum label length check for Pass 2 substring matching (already has fn.length < 3 check). Also ensure Pass 1 exact match takes priority. The current code already does this - Pass 1 exact match runs first. Verify this is working correctly and only make changes if there's an actual bug.
Step 6: Run syntax checks: unset NODE_OPTIONS && node --check server.js && node --check public/forms/PLJOB-main/lead-shared.js
acceptance_criteria: No duplicate keys in LABEL_TO_FIELD object in server.js
BL_Business form uses f_bank for agent name (consistent with all other forms)
LABEL_TO_FIELD correctly maps: 'Business Name' (capital N as written by BL) -> f_biz_name, 'Business name' (lowercase as written by PL/LAP) -> f_company
LABEL_TO_FIELD correctly maps: 'Business Address' (capital A as written by BL) -> f_biz_addr, 'Business address' (lowercase as written by PL/LAP) -> f_office_addr
node --check server.js passes with no errors
node --check public/forms/PLJOB-main/lead-shared.js passes with no errors
findings: All fixes applied successfully. Key insight: BL_Business.html uses capital 'N' in 'Business Name' and capital 'A' in 'Business Address' while PL/LAP use lowercase. This case distinction is now leveraged to route to the correct field IDs without duplicate keys. The f_agent field no longer exists - all 5 forms now use f_bank for the agent name. node --check passes for both server.js and lead-shared.js.
